coverage.assessment: The army chain, the affidavit argument, the footman setup and the Oliphant/Lady Palmerston ordering are intact. The Hugo test's reason (no ear for French verse, unwillingness to confess it) was cut in revision, so the de Musset evasion is unmotivated.
Lady Palmerston precedes Oliphant. The undefined 'two ladies' tears line from the first draft is gone. 'Of the five' and 'three young men' still resolve. Thackeray's death is framed retrospectively.
The quoted speech is intact: Cabinet Minister, Brunnow, Stirling, Milnes, Hugo. 'Then he said curtly' follows a clause whose subject is the private secretary, which invites misattribution of V6.

Russell's role remains the Minister's belief ('Perhaps he was right'). The diplomats' standard has lost 'No professional diplomatists worried about falsehoods', which leaves 'The worst liars were the candid' unsupported.
The 1862 rage and the retrospect stay distinct. The Butler retreat is not explained and the later apology is not anticipated. The Hugo anecdote is properly placed 'Ten years afterwards'.

The semicolon and dash periodicity is repeatedly broken into short sentences. The revision also drops self-deflating turns, such as the 'literary accident as strange there as one's self' and the qualification that affecting candor was 'not always a simple act'.
The foes/friends inversion and the 'getting on' irony survive. The friends' drifting apart is reduced to Swinburne alone. The Butler puzzle's explicit question was cut but is restated later.
The Milnes and Palmerston dependencies are intact at both ends. The Swinburne gulf survives locally, but the 023 revision cut its Swinburne recall.

strengths: The footman sequence keeps the Handrew and Hanthony setup intact before verbatim V4, so the climax lands.
The Thackeray episode keeps 'On quite insufficient evidence', the retrospective 1863 frame and the exact dash rhythm of V3.
The revision restored 'as helpless as an American private secretary' in the Milnes/Hugo passage. This preserves Adams's self-deprecating link to the Geneva anecdote.
The Butler episode keeps 'Perhaps he was right; at the time, his son had no doubt of it' and the unresolved betise question, as planned.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's architecture and its comic and dramatic beats. These include the foes/friends rage, the army impulse with the father's decisive argument, the muffin and 'licking' scenes, Thackeray's reproach with the exact dash punchline, the Handrew/Hanthony/Halexander sequence, the open Butler puzzle, the Swinburne night and Stirling's verdict, and the Geneva-placed Hugo anecdote. All continuity checks pass. There is no blocking defect. The revision's further cuts do some local damage. The diplomats' paradox about candor loses its premise. Adams's de Musset evasion loses its motive. The receiving line and the friends' dispersal are thinned. The draft's general sentence-splitting flattens Adams's periodic voice. One speaker attribution was already ambiguous in the source, and the first draft's split sentence makes it more so.
